name: Phi-4 Technical Report
problem: Most capable LLMs are trained on organic data; previous Phi models distilled GPT-4 and plateaued at the teacher.
mechanism: Data-quality-centred recipe with synthetic data woven through the WHOLE pipeline rather than only at the post-training step: synthetic pre-training data, synthetic reasoning traces/problems with known answers, synthetic data for post-training, plus data curriculum design and a modified post-training scheme - all on essentially the phi-3 architecture (minimal architectural change). The explicit claim is that the techniques go BEYOND distillation: the student surpasses its own teacher.
speedup_reported: Paper's own claim (abstract): phi-4 is a 14B model that, 'while previous models in the Phi family largely distill the capabilities of a teacher model (specifically GPT-4), phi-4 SUBSTANTIALLY SURPASSES ITS TEACHER MODEL on STEM-focused QA capabilities', achieving strong performance relative to its size 'especially on reasoning-focused benchmarks', with minimal architecture change from phi-3. No compression ratio or throughput figure in the abstract; the contribution is capability-per-parameter, which is an inference-cost argument by implication rather than a measured one.
